t: #2470 Number of Subarrays With LCM Equal to K
o: A subarray's LCM equals k only if every element divides k; otherwise the LCM exceeds k or fails to divide it. So for each left endpoint, extend rightward maintaining the running LCM, stopping as soon as it stops dividing k (it can only grow). Count positions where the LCM equals k. Example 1 with k=6: subarrays like [3,6], [6], [6,2], [3,6,2] qualify — 4 total. With n ≤ 1000 and k ≤ 1000, the LCM chain resets often (any element not dividing k breaks the run), keeping this near-linear in practice.
k: LCM is monotone non-decreasing as the subarray extends, and must divide k throughout.
Once the running LCM exceeds k or fails to divide k, no extension can work — break early.
gcd-based LCM: lcm(a,b) = a / gcd(a,b) * b.

a.n: Approach 1: Brute force with early termination
a.i: For each start, extend right computing running LCM; abort when it can no longer divide k; count exact matches.
s: For j ≥ i: cur = lcm(cur, nums[j]); if k % cur != 0 break; if cur == k, increment answer.
a.t: O(n²) worst case, but early breaks make it effectively O(n · d(k)) in practice since the LCM chain dies quickly.

a.i: Since the LCM only takes values dividing k (at most d(k) ≈ 32 distinct values for k ≤ 1000), keep a small map of (lcm value → leftmost index achieving it) per start; each step updates at most d(k) entries, giving O(n · d(k)) guaranteed.
s: For each i, maintain a list of (value, earliest j) pairs for LCMs of subarrays starting at i.
For each new element, transform every pair's value via lcm with nums[j], deduplicate keeping the smallest j, drop values not dividing k.
Add count of pairs with value == k.
a.t: O(n² · d(k)) worst case but with tiny constants; practically faster than it looks due to early breaks.
a.sp: O(d(k)) per start for the value map.

w: Use Approach 1 in an interview — it's short and passes comfortably. Pitfalls: overflow when multiplying LCMs (break on k % cur before it can blow up; use 64-bit in typed languages), and forgetting the strict-divisibility break condition. Follow-up: count subarrays with GCD equal to k (symmetric problem), or LCM in a range query setting (sparse table of LCMs).
